claims.text: The starting material is as-received Q235 structural steel without an intentionally applied passivation layer.
The Q235 steel may contain inherent non-metallic inclusions.
Elevated-temperature exposure promotes formation of a continuous and adherent magnetite surface film on Q235 steel.
A continuous magnetite film acts as a protective barrier that suppresses further corrosion.
Oxidation kinetics are slower at room temperature than at 70–90 °C under the proposed corrosive conditions.
Slower room-temperature oxidation produces a porous or discontinuous oxide layer.
A porous or discontinuous room-temperature oxide layer permits ongoing localized corrosion.
Temperature is the sole intended independent variable when identical coupons are exposed to the same chloride-rich medium for the same duration with humidity and oxygen availability controlled.
Elevated temperature enhances oxygen diffusion in the tested system.
Enhanced oxygen diffusion and faster oxidation kinetics favor rapid formation of a thicker, continuous magnetite film.
The elevated-temperature magnetite film adheres well to the Q235 steel substrate.
The adherent magnetite film limits anodic dissolution of iron.
Compared with room-temperature controls, elevated-temperature specimens will have a thicker and more uniform magnetite layer.
Compared with room-temperature controls, elevated-temperature specimens will have lower corrosion pit depths.
Compared with room-temperature controls, elevated-temperature specimens will have lower mass loss.
The proposed mechanism is limited to chloride-rich, static corrosive environments of moderate severity.
Different aggressive species, mechanical stresses, inclusion contents, production batches, or surface cleanliness may alter the proposed behavior.
Failure of elevated-temperature specimens to show both an improved magnetite film and reduced corrosion damage relative to room-temperature controls would falsify the proposed hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis calls the material 'pre-exposed Q235 steel,' which ordinarily implies prior exposure, while the initial-state field defines it as 'pre-exposure' and as-received. The intended starting state is therefore terminologically inconsistent.
